flags.description: In 2020 Novartis AG and its former subsidiary Alcon agreed to pay a combined $345 million to the US DOJ and SEC to resolve Foreign Corrupt Practices Act charges, admitting employees bribed government-employed healthcare providers in Greece, Vietnam and South Korea to boost sales (following a separate, smaller 2016 FCPA settlement over conduct in China).

Novartis Access, launched in 2015, offers a basket of on-patent medicines for non-communicable diseases (cardiovascular, diabetes, respiratory, breast cancer) at approximately $1 per patient per month in lower-income countries, improving treatment access where affordability is a critical barrier.
